requirements: original actual source support at x^lambda

minimal_new_actual_bridges.proof: The i-th square test uses i preceding factors and two copies of its current factor, so endpoint inflation is at most x^((i+2)tau)<=x^((R+1)tau). Existing lambda+e<=theta and delta<=e/32 allow the uniform sufficient bound (R+1)tau<=e/2.

minimal_new_actual_bridges.proof: Both pair gate coefficient sums are four. The same bound must cover the endpoint product, rather than silently using the smaller product of an individual tuple.

important_nonimplications: Finite many individual-greedy decision words do not make the corresponding tuple fibers Cartesian prime boxes. Conditions coupling group products can remain inside a fiber.

Upper-endpoint greedy gives a valid common auxiliary allocation when its budgets are paid, but generally differs from the literal per-tuple actualSelectedPairFactors decisions. An equality between these actions requires stable fit comparisons or a separate exact reorganization of the unchanged source coefficient.
One common box assignment plus real endpoint support bounds still does not prove a distribution theorem or same-policy arithmetic mean.
Existing fixed rough cutoffs giving <=11 distinct factors are specialized and should not replace the arbitrary fixed omega bound.
